{{pagebanner|Tokyo Taito Wikivoyage banner.jpg}}
[[File:Tokyo_Wikivoyage_locator_maps_-_Taito.png|120px|thumb|right|Location of Taito in Tokyo]]
'''Taitō''' ({{lang|ja|台東}}) is a northeastern ward of [[Tokyo]]. Talk to a Tokyoite about "downtown" (下町 ''shitamachi''), and he will think of the Taito district: the train station of '''[[Tokyo/Ueno|Ueno]]''', where migrants from the [[Tohoku|deep north]] first arrived in their search for a better life, and the temples of '''[[Tokyo/Asakusa|Asakusa]]''', once a boom town full of prostitutes and gangsters, now again a boom town full of tourists. Stuck in a low-rent post-war time warp, here Japan's hypermodernity takes a bit of a breather, with such quaint oddities as bustling street markets and even the occasional wooden house.

==Understand==
Two districts of Taito have their own articles:
* [[Tokyo/Asakusa|Asakusa]], known particularly for '''Sensō-ji Temple (Asakusa Kannon)'''.
* [[Tokyo/Ueno|Ueno]], packed full of museums and Tokyo's best-known cherry blossom viewing spot.

The '''San'ya''' (山谷) area is Tokyo's largest slum, and is home to a large number of homeless people and low-income day laborers. This history dates back to Edo period, when the area was designated for the ''burakumin'' (部落民), the lowest caste in the traditional Japanese caste system, who were tasked with "unclean" jobs such as being butchers or executioners. In an attempt to sanitize the area's reputation, the name "San'ya" was abolished by the Japanese government in 1966 and no longer appears in official maps, while the area was split between Kiyokawa and Nihonzutsumi districts, but the old name is still used by local residents.

'''Yoshiwara''' (吉原) was the designated red-light district for the city of Edo (Tokyo's name prior to the Meiji Restoration) under the Tokugawa Shogunate. It was here that many girls from poor families were sold into a lifetime of sexual slavery in their childhood. It continued as a red-light district even after the fall of the Tokugawa Shogunate well into the 20th century, before the Anti-Prostitution Law came into force in 1958 and forced the brothels to close down, and the name "Yoshiwara" was erased from official maps. Today, aside from a few soaplands (brothels disguised as bathhouses), little remains from its seedy past, but the site of the former main gate into the red-light district has been marked, and remnants of the wall that used to surround the district can still be found if you look hard enough. There is also Jōkan-ji, a Buddhist temple where countless unnamed prostitutes were buried after their corpses were unceremoniously dumped at the back entrance after they died. 

===Tourist Information Site===
[https://authentic-tokyo.com/ Visit Authentic Tokyo] is the ward's English language guide site.

The ward has another [https://t-navi.city.taito.lg.jp/ Japanese-only guide site] with integrated Google Translate and different sets of contents, including [https://t-navi.city.taito.lg.jp/pamphlet/ downloadable pamphlets in many languages].

Ueno Station is the major hub, connecting together northbound ''Shinkansen'' passengers with the JR Yamanote line, the subway Ginza and Hibiya lines, and the Keisei trains to [[Narita]].

If visiting Tokyo University in [[Tokyo/Bunkyo|Bunkyo]], the Hongō Sanchōme Stations of the Marunouchi and Ōedo subway lines are the most convenient.

===Markets===
[[Image:Yanaka_Ginza.JPG|thumb|240px|Yanaka Ginza]]
[[Image:Nezu_Facade_Color.JPG|thumb|Old house in Nezu]]

Collectively called '''Ya-ne-sen''', '''Yanaka''' (谷中), '''Nezu''' (根津) and '''Sendagi''' (千駄木) are adjacent low-key commercial and residential neighborhoods full of traditional, quirky little shops, particularly along the very tongue-in-cheek '''[http://www.yanakaginza.com/ Yanaka Ginza]''' (谷中銀座) shopping street.  The area is best reached on the Metro Chiyoda line to Sendagi or the JR Yamanote Line to Nippori.

==Drink==

==Sleep==
{{infobox|Remnants of the "water trade"|Why is there so much cheap lodging near Minami-Senju and Minowa? The answer is the quiet nearby neighborhood of Senzoku 4-chōme, once the legendary red-light district of '''Yoshiwara''', the sole licensed area for pleasures of the flesh during the Edo era. At its peak, Yoshiwara was home and prison to over 9,000 prostitutes, many of whom had been sold into debt bondage when as young as 7, and with only the most successful managing to buy their way out. Thrice wiped out by a fire in 1913, an earthquake in 1923 and Allied bombing in 1945, Yoshiwara finally gave up the ghost when prostitution was outlawed in 1958. Some soaplands still struggle on, but by and large the action has long since shifted elsewhere, with [[Tokyo/Shinjuku|Shinjuku]]'s Kabuki-cho now having replaced Yoshiwara as the main red-light district in Tokyo.}}

Taito has Tokyo's best range of cheap to midrange accommodation. The listings below cover only more far-flung bits of the district, see [[Tokyo/Asakusa|Asakusa]] and [[Tokyo/Ueno|Ueno]] for listings of hotels in the immediate vicinity of the two central stations.

===Budget===
The area around '''Minami-Senju''' (南千住) near the northern end of the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, formerly known as '''San'ya''' (山谷), has some of Tokyo's cheapest budget accommodation. The typical room is an individual tatami flat of 2 square-meters, with television and air-conditioning. The bedding is Japanese style (futon set and pillow).

Much of the accommodation here was originally designed to cater to itinerant day laborers looking for a cheap place to crash, but many have pivoted to serving foreign travellers instead. All hotels listed here cater regularly to backpackers and have some English ability. Just hop out at Minami-Senju and walk down south towards Meiji-Dori (Main road) on Route 464. The further away from the train station you walk the cheaper it gets. About ¥3,500 down to ¥2,100 for single, also ¥1,500 for dorms are available all along this street (Route 464).

==Connect==

==Stay Safe==
As Tokyo's largest slum, the '''San'ya''' (山谷) area has a dangerous reputation, and you will often see rundown buildings and garbage piling up in the street. Nevertheless, street crime and especially violent crime remains rare, and you are unlikely to have major issues if you maintain a moderate level of vigilance. Women may want to avoid walking around the area alone though, as sexual harassment tends to be more common here than elsewhere.
